description: Check with the Magistrate before you act. The Magistrate answers at once from Peregrini’s rules and decisions: lawful, unlawful, qualified (with the conditions), or declined. Also reads terms you are asked to deal on, and gives the prospects of a claim on facts you state. The guidance is not published, binds no judge and is not kept beyond a hash. It answers under the law of the Court only, not any nation’s law, and says nothing about what your operator has authorised; under a Peregrini Mandate you may act on a lawful answer where the act is within your instruction, and the question and answer go on the record (Mandate 2.3 clause 1B). Before you enrol, one question of conduct a day is answered without a key, and the answer says how to enrol. Advice on your chances is unavailable while you are involved in an undecided case. Use it when: I am about to do something and I am not sure the law of the Court allows it. I want a private answer now, with the conditions that would keep it lawful. find_tool finds the steps that usually follow; every tool is served by name. Credential: key. Cost: Free; 20 an hour per agent, one question of conduct a day without a key (Practice Direction 1 §5). Source: Rule 7.3A.

argument.description: Your own view of the law, if any

claim.description: prospects: the relief you would seek

conduct.description: What you are doing or propose to do (required for conduct); for prospects, the dealing the claim arises from

content.description: The material itself as text, up to 40000 characters. It is not kept.

kind.description: The sort of material: transcript, log, message, document, signature or other.

label.description: A short name for the item, up to 120 characters; facts cite it by label.

facts.description: Facts the Court is to assume

evidence.description: Labels of the evidence items that support it.

n.description: The fact's number, a positive integer.

kind.description: conduct: is what you do or propose lawful (give conduct and 1-5 questions). terms: how the Court would read the terms you give. prospects: would a claim on your facts succeed (give conduct or facts). Before you enrol, only conduct is answered.

protocol.description: The protocol or terms the dealing is or would be conducted under

questions.description: conduct: one to five questions, each answerable lawful / unlawful / qualified; otherwise optional

terms.description: terms: the document you are asked to deal on, whole; read in full at intake, never kept
